decision: Phase 3 is done when a reviewer can score and note an applicant, an admin can confirm only a sheet-legal move through applyDecision, the preview matches the queued email, bulk results are per row, and a sheet row cannot silently replace a staff decision
why: The operator asked for a falsifiable review workflow on the existing decision path, with no public-site changes and no new state machine

decision: Rigor is high. Migration 0016, the actor on applyDecision, and sheet coexistence are one-way doors. Nominations and partners wait until the review loop is verified
why: A wrong decision emails an applicant or overwrites the spreadsheet. The operator said refuse and surface a real conflict

decision: Dashboard status changes will call applyDecision, never performAction. performAction can mark round 1 complete and reprovision identity
why: Those ops actions skip VideoAsk and Didit. The operator forbade exposing them

decision: A stale sheet decision can apply on the next tick after pull copies the new version onto the row, because stale writes no receipt and decisionHash ignores version
why: Push runs before pull. Team columns survive the pull. The second push then sees a matching version and the old decision cells

decision: Applicant detail is read-only. There is no assignee column. reviewer on the row is free text, not a user id. admin_events.subject_id can only point at a staff user
why: Assignment and per-cycle notes need their own rows. Staff audit of a review stores the applicant id in the event detail, not in subject_id

decision: Seeing the queue is dashboard.read. The reviewer role cannot write. A confirm capability has to be added to the map, and the detail loader must select version
why: The operator said not to hard-code role names. The page today does not even load the version a decision needs

decision: A sheet retry after a stale push can apply once pull has copied the new version onto the row, because stale writes no receipt and the hash ignores version
why: The cron writes decisionId before applyDecision. The next tick retries that id against the refreshed version and the old yellow cells

decision: Preview must call decisionEmail with the same status, link, locale, and sources the queue will store. It must not call queueDecisionEmail, which mints a switch-online token
why: The worker sends the stored job payload and does not render again. A second queue call is deduped and keeps the first token

decision: The dashboard may offer only the 13 moves that pass targetStatus, decisionSourceStatuses, and TRANSITIONS. It will not call performAction
why: Ops can mark round 1 complete and reprovision identity. A not_allowed applyDecision still stores the receipt, so a confirm must send only the one field for that move

decision: The explanation matches the code. Thirteen sheet moves succeed. online_offered and interview_yes are not among them. A stale sheet row can apply on the next tick after pull refreshes version
why: The explainer corrected the allowFrom lists against TRANSITIONS and kept the attachment point at applyDecision

decision: Two design sketches are running from the same brief, one Opus and one Grok, writing only under /tmp/arena-admin-phase3
why: The actor change, the sheet refuse rule, and where notes live are one-way doors. Two whole shapes before any code

decision: Grok sketch stores scores apart from the sheet, requires a decision origin, and holds a later sheet row when a staff receipt for this cycle disagrees on status
why: A note must not bump version. A webhook bump must still let the sheet apply. The hold compares status, not the decision hash

decision: The Opus sketch stopped before writing any files because that model was out of usage
why: A second whole shape is still required. The replacement is a first-party model, same brief, its own directory

decision: Base is the Grok sketch. No grafts from Composer. The judge scored 30 to 15 and the parent agrees
why: Composer writes a receipt on every stale push, which stops the sheet from applying after a webhook bumps version. It also defaults the channel to excel and reuses decision words for recommendations

decision: The review desk matches the Grok sketch. A real click on Confirm applies the move and opens the next applicant
why: The cookie banner covered Confirm when the decision card was taller than the viewport. The card now scrolls inside the desk column, and a mouse click on Confirm landed on the button
